correctness.rationale: Fu–Xie–Li Proposition 2.1 gives the nonstandard bridge D(X)DW_S(X)=2. For the inradius-one regular N=4n polygon, the radial function is R(theta)=sec d(theta), with facet normals spaced by 2alpha and alpha=pi/N. The symmetric-plane orthogonality lemma reduces all unit isosceles pairs to a quarter-turn pair. Writing delta=arctan(lambda) yields the exact objective cos d(theta+delta)/(cos d(theta) cos delta). After reduction to theta,epsilon in [-alpha,alpha] and an integer facet shift m, the proof treats m=0, |m|=1, and |m|>=2 exhaustively. All three regions have lower bound 2cos(alpha)/(1+cos(alpha)); theta=delta=alpha/2 attains it. The published bridge therefore gives DW_S=1+sec(alpha).
risks: The quarter-turn description depends on the regular 4n-gon being a symmetric Minkowski plane with perpendicular facet-normal axes; this is stated explicitly in the proof.
Finite numerical checks are not used to prove the universal quantifier over n.

value.rationale: DW_S was introduced specifically to quantify how a norm departs from Hilbert geometry under Singer orthogonality. The finding gives a closed formula for an infinite canonical family rather than one isolated polygon and shows a clean geometric interpolation from the square extremum 1+sqrt(2) to the Hilbert value 2. The equivalent exact formula for D(X) also quantifies the isosceles-to-Birkhoff discrepancy on every regular 4n-gonal plane. The proof isolates a reusable radial/facet-shift mechanism for other polygonal orthogonality constants.
risks: The theorem covers only the quarter-turn-symmetric even-polygon residue class and is not a complete classification for all regular even polygons.
